title: Leading a band from the drums
summary: He explains how he led as a drummer: giving the downbeat, chording, adding bars, and sitting in the middle so everyone could see.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Now, that was the first time that you were a bandleader.
At the Deléssa, right, right.
Yeah, and you turned into quite a bandleader, a real leader --
Well, --
And that's rare for a drummer.

Right, right, but the only -- it was great. I mean, it was great for the simple reason that first thing happened was, when I went in, I didn't go in as a leader. I mean, within my own self. I said, now, I'm the leader of
this band, but we're all -- been knowing each other and been playing together, so I'm just like a sideman, you know?
Yeah.

So that was the attitude that I had. And then it was so much more easier for me to do the job, as a leader, than it was for another instrument, because they'd have to stop tempos and all that, I could just go right with the downbeat and was gone.
(Unintelligible).
Right, right, right, see, so everything worked out very well as a drum leader.
Well, how did you -- did somebody else give the downbeat or --
No, no, all that come from me. Everything came from me. Yeah.
How would you do that?

Well, here's the thing. It was a chording. Very few things I would stomp off, but other things, I mean, I could just give them a downbeat or else I'd add four bars in front or something like that. And this type of a thing. So you had the freedom, the freedom that you weren't restricted with conductor and all that type of a thing. So that's beautiful for a drummer.
Yeah, right.
Right.
I used to have a show band, play shows.
Yeah.
And it was always hard to get a downbeat if I was sitting in the back.
No, no, right, right. But I didn't. I always sat in the middle.
You sat in the middle?
Right in front. You understand what I mean? In the middle and so all they had to --
Where everybody could see you.
Where everybody could see you, right.
That makes sense.
Yeah, right.
